content:
The image shows a corn leaf that is predominantly healthy and green. The key observation is a single small, white/cream-colored circular spot on the leaf surface. The rest of the leaf tissue appears undamaged with no visible lesions, pustules, streaks, or other abnormalities.

**Analysis:**
- Single small, white-cream, roughly circular spot on an otherwise green leaf
- No pustules (rules out Common_rust, Southern_rust)
- No elongated lesions (rules out Northern_corn_leaf_blight, Gray_leaf_spot)
- No banding, streaking, or mosaic (rules out viral diseases)
- No tar-like raised spots (rules out Tar_spot)

The small, isolated white/tan circular spot is most consistent with **Holcus spot** — caused by *Pseudomonas syringae* pv. *holci*, which produces round to elliptical, tan to white spots roughly 1/8 to 1/4 inch in diameter. These spots can start near the leaf and appear on otherwise healthy-looking tissue.
